run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: Yes — recent logs for app-102b/traffic-manager contain one error-level line. Loki returned exactly one ERROR record for the namespace in 2026-11-23T18:00:00Z–19:02:26Z: on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-cgpvv at 2026-11-23T19:02:19.000Z, {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}. Everything else in that window is normal access-log traffic (150 JSON request lines from the three pods at 19:02:19.001–.050 with statuses 200, 201 and 204); a filter for status 5xx in the namespace returned only this same error line. The workload itself is not degraded as far as the evidence goes: Deployment app-102b/traffic-manager is 3/3 ready, all three pods are Running with restartCount 0, no last-termination/OOMKilled state, and the single container's own stdout read from the kubelet holds only nginx startup notices (23 lines per pod, no error lines, no previous container instance). The deployment and its pods were created at 2026-11-23T19:02:17Z (generation 1, revision 1, image nginx:latest), so only about nine seconds of log history existed at query time. The container declares no resources requests/limits (resources {}), the namespace has no ResourceQuota, no NetworkPolicy, no Service and no Endpoints object, so the log's claim of 'Memory requests above 90%' has no configured memory request to correspond to in the cluster config; the actual memory usage could not be checked because Prometheus was unreachable during this Run. The line's provenance is also inconsistent: it carries container="nginx", level="ERROR" and detected_level="error" labels and a whole-second timestamp, yet it does not appear in the container log stream read for that pod. The cause is therefore not established.

claims.text: Deployment app-102b/traffic-manager exists with 3 replicas, 3 ready, 3 available, 3 updated, image nginx:latest, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1, created 2026-11-23T19:02:17Z, generation 1, applied by manager kubectl-client-side-apply; its single container is named nginx (containerPort 80) with empty resources ({}), no env, no livenessProbe and no readinessProbe.

Loki returned exactly one error-level log line for namespace app-102b in 2026-11-23T18:00:00Z–19:02:26Z: pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-cgpvv, container nginx, timestamp 2026-11-23T19:02:19.000Z, line {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}.

The only other logs returned for namespace app-102b in that window are 150 JSON access-log lines from the three traffic-manager pods (traffic-manager-585c5579f6-cgpvv, -gnhsh, -jr7hx) timestamped 2026-11-23T19:02:19.001–.050 with HTTP statuses 200, 201 and 204; a line-filter for status 5xx in the namespace matched only the single ERROR line above, no access-log entry.

The three traffic-manager pods are Running on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, created 2026-11-23T19:02:17Z, all conditions (PodReadyToStartContainers, Initialized, Ready, ContainersReady, PodScheduled) True, container nginx ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination state; their owner is ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6.

Kubelet container logs for all three pods contain only nginx startup output (23 lines each: docker-entrypoint configuration, nginx/1.31.9 start, 8 worker processes); cgpvv's stream ends at 2026-11-23T19:02:18.363733Z, gnhsh's at 19:02:19.193236Z, jr7hx's at 19:02:18.783723Z, each with no previous container instance and no error/alert line, so the 19:02:19.000Z ERROR line is not present in the container log stream read for that pod.

Namespace app-102b contains no Service and no Endpoints object, no ResourceQuota and no NetworkPolicy at query time; the cluster has only one deployment whose name matches 'traffic' (app-102b/traffic-manager), and only three pods carry label app=nginx, all in app-102b.

Namespace app-102b events in the events window (2026-11-23T19:02:17Z–19:02:19Z) are all Normal: Deployment traffic-manager ScalingReplicaSet 'from 0 to 3', three ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 SuccessfulCreate, and for each pod Scheduled/Pulling/Pulled/Created/Started; there is no FailedScheduling, Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy or back-off event for these pods.

The string 'Memory requests above 90%' appeared in only one namespace across the whole window in Loki (10-minute count by namespace over 18:40:00Z–19:02:26Z returned a single series, namespace app-102b, value 1).

Against calling the workload damaged: all three pods are Ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason, the deployment reports 3/3 ready and available, and the kubelet container logs of all three pods contain only normal nginx startup output with no error, panic or OOM line.

Rejected as unrelated to this question: the Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events 'endpoints "loki" already exists' (namespaces app-100a, app-101, app-102) and 'endpoints "mariadb" already exists' (namespace app-219) involve Services loki and mariadb in other namespaces, not traffic-manager in app-102b, and no such object exists in app-102b.

The 'Memory alert' text is emitted by the workload/application layer rather than derived from a real cluster memory constraint: the container declares no memory request or limit (resources {}), the namespace has no ResourceQuota, and no pod shows OOMKilled or a restart. Its status field 501 does not match any access-log entry — the observed access-log statuses are only 200, 201 and 204 — so it cannot be tied to a specific failed request.

The ERROR line may come from a different ingestion path than the pod's kubelet log stream: unlike the 150 access-log lines it carries container="nginx", level="ERROR" and detected_level="error" labels, its timestamp is exactly 19:02:19.000000000Z (whole second) while neighbouring lines carry millisecond timestamps, and it is absent from the container log stream read from the kubelet for the same pod.

Because the alert text asks for more memory, the human follow-up worth doing is to confirm the container's real memory working set against its budget (the deployment currently sets no request/limit) using kubelet/cAdvisor memory metrics, and to check whether the 501-status 'Memory alert' line recurs over a longer log window before treating it as an ongoing fault.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_metric_names both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (three attempts), so container memory working set, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube-state-metrics series and any Prometheus-side error rate for app-102b/traffic-manager could not be checked; missing series are unknown, not zero.

Log history for this workload is only about nine seconds long at query time: the Deployment and its ReplicaSet/pods were created 2026-11-23T19:02:17Z and no earlier pods or previous container instances exist, so whether the 'Memory alert' line recurs, and how long it has been occurring, is unknown; Kubernetes events returned cover only 18:27:05Z–19:02:19Z, so an earlier deleted deployment of the same name cannot be ruled out from events.

The ERROR line at 2026-11-23T19:02:19.000Z is not present in the container log stream read from the kubelet for pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-cgpvv (that stream ends 19:02:18.363733Z); the reason for the discrepancy could not be determined.
No LimitRange object was examined because the resource kind is not available to these tools, and Secrets cannot be read; neither could be ruled out as a source of a memory setting.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so who created/edited Deployment app-102b/traffic-manager at 19:02:17Z beyond the kubectl-client-side-apply manager label is unknown.
No Service or Endpoints object exists in app-102b, so how the 150 access-log requests reached these pods (client IPs 10.0.x.x) was not determined.
next_steps: Check container memory usage versus limit for app-102b/traffic-manager pods once Prometheus is reachable (e.g. container_memory_working_set_bytes / kube_pod_container_resource_limits) and compare pods cgpvv, gnhsh and jr7hx.
Re-query Loki for {namespace="app-102b"} |= "Memory alert" over a longer window after the pods have run longer, to see whether the ERROR recurs and whether it correlates with 5xx responses.
Ask the workload owner what emits the 'Memory alert' / status 501 message, since the container runs stock nginx:latest and no fault-injecting ConfigMap or setting exists in app-102b.
Consider adding memory requests/limits and probes to the traffic-manager container if it is intended to be protected by a memory budget.
